# Validation report (simulated)

**Every number in this report comes from a simulation.** There is no board.
The figures are what the behavioural model of the converter and front end
produces when the host analysis tools are run on its output, the same tools
that would run on a real capture. They show that the design, the
measurement methods and the firmware hang together; they are not
measurements and they say nothing about a real part's INL, drift or
layout. The bench procedure that would replace them is in
[calibration_procedure.md](calibration_procedure.md).

## The simulated board

One board instance, drawn once with a fixed seed from the tolerances in the
bill of materials (0.1 % resistors, reference initial accuracy 0.05 %,
amplifier and converter offsets within +/-15 uV and +/-40 uV):

| Nominal gain | Actual gain of this instance |
|---|---|
| 1 | 1.000000 |
| 8 | 7.962600 |
| 32 | 31.737875 |
| 128 | 127.971804 |

Gain stage offset -7.30 uV, converter offset
-24.05 uV, reference 2.500125 V. The
static non-linearity is an assumed bow of 1 ppm and S curve
of 2 ppm of FSR, of the order a good 24-bit part specifies.

## Noise floor (input shorted)

2048 conversions per gain at 2400 SPS. Input referred, uV rms.
Effective bits are log2(FSR / rms); noise free bits use a 6.6 sigma peak to peak.

| Gain | Simulated | Budget | Target | Simulated / budget | Effective bits | Noise free bits | Target |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.601 | 0.644 | 0.75 | 0.933 | 22.99 | 20.27 | meets |
| 8 | 0.260 | 0.252 | 0.40 | 1.032 | 21.20 | 18.48 | meets |
| 32 | 0.227 | 0.233 | 0.32 | 0.974 | 19.39 | 16.67 | meets |
| 128 | 0.234 | 0.230 | 0.30 | 1.015 | 17.35 | 14.63 | meets |

The simulation and the budget agree to within a few percent, about the
spread expected of a 2048 sample record, except at gain 1
where the simulated floor is lower: the budget's linear model of the 1-bit quantiser
over-estimates its noise, which is the conservative direction.

## Sine wave tests (IEEE 1241 methods)

Coherent sampling, 4096 samples, 67 cycles, no window. SINAD and ENOB
come from a four parameter sine fit, SNR, THD and SFDR from the spectrum with
harmonics 2 to 9 excluded from noise.

| Gain | f (Hz) | Level (dBFS) | SNR (dB) | Budget SNR (dB) | THD (dB) | SFDR (dB) | SINAD (dB) | ENOB | ENOB, IEEE 1241 (FSR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 39.258 | -1.02 | 127.42 | 126.91 | -118.52 | 121.05 | 117.99 | 19.31 | 19.47 |
| 128 | 39.258 | -1.02 | 94.35 | 94.57 | -112.72 | 115.69 | 94.29 | 15.37 | 15.54 |

At gain 1 against the targets: SNR 127.4 dB meets
120 dB, THD -118.5 dB meets
-110 dB and ENOB 19.31 meets
19 bits. The ENOB is set by distortion, which is set by the
assumed INL; with noise alone it would be 20.87 bits.

## Linearity

A 41 point DC sweep from -95 % to +95 % of full scale at gain 1,
32 conversions averaged per point.

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Peak INL, best fit line | 1.24 ppm of FSR |
| Peak INL, end point line | 1.38 ppm of FSR |
| Non-linearity the model was given, best fit | 1.22 ppm of FSR |
| Target | 5 ppm of FSR: meets |

This is a test of the measurement, not of a converter: the sweep recovers
the non-linearity the model was given, to within the averaged noise.

## Calibration against simulated references

Two points per gain: input shorted, then the simulated calibrator at 0.9 of
full scale (assumed accuracy +/-2 ppm of setting). Then eleven points from
-90 % to +90 % of full scale, each read by the DAQ and by the simulated
reference DMM (assumed +/-3 ppm of reading +/-0.2 uV). Errors in ppm of FSR.
"Against truth" is only possible in a simulation.

| Gain | offset_q8 | gain_q29 | Worst before | Worst after, against DMM | Worst after, against truth | Target |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | -31372 | 536896937 | 29.2 | 2.90 | 1.85 | meets |
| 8 | -75400 | 539418625 | 2143.3 | 2.81 | 2.06 | meets |
| 32 | -225292 | 541331474 | 3760.4 | 2.12 | 1.89 | meets |
| 128 | -826804 | 537016852 | 315.7 | 4.84 | 1.41 | meets |

These coefficients come from the Python reference implementation. The
firmware in the loop run repeats the calibration in the C firmware on fresh
codes from the model and checks its coefficients and every calibrated sample
against the Python implementation, bit for bit; see
[test-results/calibration/firmware_in_loop.csv](../test-results/calibration/firmware_in_loop.csv).
